tasks.title: A function with checkable examples
tasks.statement: Write fizzbuzz(n): for n divisible by 15 return "FizzBuzz"; divisible by 3, "Fizz"; divisible by 5, "Buzz"; otherwise the number as a string. In the docstring give at least four examples in doctest format (>>> ...), and all of them must pass.
tasks.hint: In the docstring: >>> fizzbuzz(15), and on the next line 'FizzBuzz' (with quotes, as the repr of a string).

tasks.title: Table-driven tests
tasks.statement: Write run_cases(func, cases): cases is a list of pairs (arguments, expected), where arguments is a tuple. Return a list of failure descriptions in the order of the cases, in the form "func(args): expected X, got Y" (with the real argument tuple, expected value and actual value); if the function raised an exception, use "func(args): exception TypeName". Skip the cases that pass.
tasks.hint: for args, want in cases: try: got = func(*args) except Exception as e: ...; if got != want: ...

tasks.title: A test with Mock
tasks.statement: The function greet(user_id, fetch) returns "Hello, <name>", where the name is obtained by calling fetch(user_id). Write check_greet(): create a Mock (unittest.mock) with return_value="Ann", call greet(7, mock), check the result and that the mock was called exactly once with the argument 7; return True if everything is correct and False otherwise.
tasks.hint: fetch = Mock(return_value="Ann"); text = greet(7, fetch); fetch.assert_called_once_with(7) inside try/except AssertionError.

tasks.title: Setting up logging
tasks.statement: Write setup_logger(stream): a logger named "app" with level INFO and a single handler writing to stream in the format "LEVEL:message" (%(levelname)s:%(message)s). Calling it again must not add a second handler. Turn off propagation of records to parent loggers.
tasks.hint: logger = logging.getLogger("app"); if there are no handlers, add a StreamHandler(stream) with a Formatter; level INFO; propagate = False.

tasks.title: An application exception hierarchy
tasks.statement: Create the exceptions AppError(Exception), NotFound(AppError) and ValidationError(AppError). NotFound takes an entity name and a key and builds the message "<entity> not found: <key>"; ValidationError stores the field (attribute field) and a message. Write find_user(users, user_id): it returns the user from the dict or raises NotFound("user", user_id).
tasks.hint: NotFound.__init__(self, entity, key): super().__init__(f"{entity} not found: {key}"); for ValidationError the message is f"{field}: {message}" and also store self.field.

tasks.title: Discounts as strategies
tasks.statement: Write make_discount(spec): from a string, return a price function. "none" means no discount; "percent:10" is a 10% discount (round the result to two decimal places, round(..., 2)); "fixed:5" subtracts 5 but not below zero. An unknown scheme raises ValueError.
tasks.hint: kind, _, arg = spec.partition(":"); for each kind return its own function (a closure over the number).

tasks.title: An event bus
tasks.statement: Write EventBus: subscribe(event, handler), unsubscribe(event, handler) and emit(event, *args), which calls the event's handlers in the order they subscribed and returns their count. Unsubscribing a handler that is not subscribed must not fail. Subscribing the same function twice calls it twice.
tasks.hint: A dict of event to list of handlers; in unsubscribe remove the first occurrence (list.remove) with try/except ValueError.

tasks.title: Rewrite it the Python way
tasks.statement: The function pairs_report(names, scores) works correctly but is written with indexes (range(len(...)), building the list by hand). Rewrite it idiomatically, with zip and a comprehension, without range(len(...)) and without the append method. The result: strings "<name>: <score>" for scores of at least 50.
tasks.hint: return [f"{n}: {s}" for n, s in zip(names, scores) if s >= 50].

tasks.title: A mini property check
tasks.statement: Write check_property(prop, gen, trials=200, seed=0): create random.Random(seed), and trials times call gen(rng) to get an input and prop(input); return the first input for which prop returned a false value (or raised an exception), or None if no counterexample was found.
tasks.hint: rng = random.Random(seed); for _ in range(trials): case = gen(rng); try: ok = prop(case) except Exception: return case; if not ok: return case; at the end return None.
